title: On the coincidence of discrete and continuous definitions of Entanglement of Formation
authors: Haobo Ma, Maksim E. Shirokov, Wenlin Zhang
abstract: It is proved that every Borel ensemble of pure states on a separable bipartite Hilbert space with finite average entanglement admits a countable ensemble with the same barycenter and arbitrarily small additional average entanglement. Consequently, the discrete and continuous versions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide on the whole space of states of infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum system (with infinite values allowed).   The main idea of the proof (realized with the AI-assistance) is the identification of a Borel ensemble of pure bipartite states with a Borel probability measure on the unit sphere of the space of Hilbert--Schmidt operators followed by dividing the support of this measure into appropriate cells and replacing each cell by its conditional barycenter. The resulting countable ensemble is obtained by a recursive construction.
summary: This paper proves that the discrete and continuous definitions of the Entanglement of Formation coincide for infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum systems. The authors achieve this by developing a powerful discretization theorem that allows any continuous ensemble to be approximated arbitrarily closely by a countable ensemble. This result unifies the mathematical treatment of entanglement measures in complex quantum settings.
main_problem: The paper aims to prove the mathematical coincidence between two definitions of the Entanglement of Formation (EoF) for infinite-dimensional bipartite quantum systems: the discrete version (based on countable decompositions) and the continuous version (based on Borel probability measures).
main_result: The core result is the equality $E_d^F(ho) = E_c^F(ho)$ for all bipartite states $ho$, establishing that the continuous definition does not yield a lower bound below that achievable by countable ensembles.
method: The proof employs an 'exact discretization theorem' by mapping the continuous ensemble to a Borel measure on Hilbert-Schmidt operators, which is then recursively partitioned and approximated by a countable ensemble.
model_or_system: The system involves bipartite quantum states $ho$ on separable Hilbert spaces $H_A \otimes H_B$. The analysis is formalized using the representation of pure states via Hilbert-Schmidt operators $A \in \mathcal{S}_2(H_B, H_A)$.
key_observables: Entanglement of Formation ($E^F$), Entanglement Entropy ($S(\cdot)$), and the associated cost functional $J(A)$.
important_parameters: The proof involves taking a limit $\eta 	o 0$ and relies on contraction factors $\alpha = \eta/4$ and $\eta/2$ during the recursive decomposition.
main_assumptions: The proof assumes the existence of a Borel section for lifting the measure $\mu$ to a probability measure $\mu_0$, and it requires the cost functional $J$ to be convex and lower semicontinuous.
paper_structure: The paper develops the proof by first establishing the necessary discretization theorem (Theorem 1), then formalizing the continuous ensemble as a Borel measure on amplitudes, and finally applying a recursive decomposition process (Lemma 5) to show that the total cost converges to the discrete definition's value.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous mathematical grounding for entanglement measures in infinite dimensions, which is crucial for developing robust quantum information protocols that rely on these quantities.
